claim: Tissue resident macrophages (TRMs) are phagocytic immune cells that contribute to organogenesis and tissue homeostasis.
source: Tissue resident macrophages (TRMs) are phagocytic immune cells that also contribute to organogenesis and tissue homeostasis.

source: Therefore, perturbations in TRM production or activity can have detrimental consequences ranging from abnormal organ development to neurodegeneration and cancer (Cassetta and Pollard, 2018; Mass et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2018; Zarif et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In vertebrates, TRMs derive from successive waves of hematopoiesis that initiate early during development.
source: In vertebrates, including mammals, birds, and fishes, TRMs derive from successive waves of hematopoiesis that initiate early during development reviewed in: McGrath et al. (2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a review.

claim: The initial two embryonic waves give rise to primitive macrophages born in the embryonic yolk sac in mammals and birds or the rostral blood island (RBI) in fishes.
source: The initial two embryonic waves give rise to primitive macrophages, born in the embryonic yolk sac in mammals and birds or the rostral blood island (RBI) in fishes
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about hematopoiesis.

claim: Erythro-myeloid precursors (EMPs) originate in the yolk sac and expand in the fetal liver of mammals or emerge from the posterior blood island (PBI) of fishes.
source: and erythro-myeloid precursors (EMPs), which also originate in the yolk sac and expand in the fetal liver of mammals or emerge from the posterior blood island (PBI) of fishes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: A third embryonic wave generates definitive hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that begin in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros (AGM) region.
source: A third embryonic wave that generates definitive hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) begins in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros (AGM) region, where HSCs bud from the hemogenic endothelium (Bertrand et al., 2010; Boisset et al., 2010; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010).

claim: In zebrafish, newly born HSCs migrate to the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) and later seed hematopoietic organs such as the kidney marrow.
source: In zebrafish, newly born hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) migrate to the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT), and later seed hematopoietic organs such as the kidney marrow, which is equivalent to the bone marrow in mammals (Henninger et al., 2017; Murayama et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Most TRM populations are established by the end of fetal life and are subsequently maintained through the proliferation of local progenitors or through the partial contribution of bone marrow-derived cells.

claim: During their colonization of the embryo, macrophages acquire distinct properties adapted to their microenvironment.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The ontogeny of TRMs within a specific organ is heterogeneous and thought to be determined by the availability of the niche and accessibility of the host tissue.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a review.

claim: The microenvironment has a major role in determining TRM phenotype and function, largely regardless of ontogeny.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Colony stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R) is an evolutionarily conserved regulator of macrophage development.
source: Colony stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R) is an evolutionarily conserved regulator of macrophage development, directly inducing DNA and protein synthesis as well as proliferation upon ligand binding (Hume et al., 2016; Tushinski and Stanley, 1985).

claim: CSF1R directly induces DNA and protein synthesis as well as proliferation upon ligand binding.
source: Colony stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R) is an evolutionarily conserved regulator of macrophage development, directly inducing DNA and protein synthesis as well as proliferation upon ligand binding (Hume et al., 2016; Tushinski and Stanley, 1985).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Recessive and dominant mutations in CSF1R can cause severe brain disease.
